answer: The U.S. unemployment rate in April 2020 was 14.8% (seasonally adjusted). That is the current revised figure. BLS first reported 14.7%. Source: BLS, via FRED series UNRATE.
The U.S. unemployment rate in October 2009 was 10.0% (seasonally adjusted), the peak of the Great Recession period. Source: BLS, via FRED series UNRATE.

The highest weekly 30-year fixed mortgage rate in 1981 was 18.63%, in the week of October 9, 1981. It is also the all-time high of the survey. Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, via FRED series MORTGAGE30US.
The 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield on March 9, 2020 was 0.54%. It had been 0.74% on March 6 and was 0.76% on March 10. Source: Federal Reserve Board H.15, via FRED series DGS10.

Year-over-year headline CPI inflation in June 2022 was about 9.0%, using the seasonally adjusted CPI-U index (294.957 in June 2022 against 270.654 in June 2021, which works out to 8.98%). BLS's headline figure, which uses the non-seasonally-adjusted index, was 9.1%. Source: BLS, via FRED series CPIAUCSL. The percentage is my calculation from the index levels.

Housing starts in January 2006 were 2,273,000 units at a seasonally adjusted annual rate (2,273 thousand). That was the housing-boom peak. Source: U.S. Census Bureau/HUD New Residential Construction, via FRED series HOUST.

The lowest monthly reading of the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index in 2022 was 50.0, in June 2022. It was the record low for the series. Source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, via FRED series UMCSENT.

The WTI crude oil spot price (Cushing, OK) on April 20, 2020 was -$36.98 per barrel. That is negative, the first negative price on record. Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, via FRED series DCOILWTICO.

The U.S. personal saving rate in April 2020 was 31.8% of disposable personal income (seasonally adjusted annual rate), in the current revised data. Earlier vintages showed different values, such as 33.7% at first release. Source: BEA, via FRED series PSAVERT.

Real GDP in Q2 2020 fell at a -28.0% seasonally adjusted annualized rate, in the current revised data. Earlier estimates were larger: -32.9% at the advance estimate and later -31.4%. Source: BEA, via FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA.
